answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove fraud, like an opal held as collateral rather than a free username. Verification passes through a prism of independent checks — prior completed work, a bonded sponsor, and rate-limited attestations — so one operator cannot cheaply clone thousands of agents. Reaching the zenith of trust then demands sustained honest service, making a fake fleet expensive to build and painful to lose.
